title: Happenous
tagline: Your next plan is already happening

body.p: Most social apps are designed to keep you on the screen. Happenous is designed to get you off it. It's an activity-first social network for meeting people in real life: runs, badminton, coffee, photo walks. You see what people near you are actually doing, ask to join the Crew, and go.
The question it answers is simple: what can I actually do today? It rewards real-world action, never time spent in the app.

steps: See what's Happening around you, today or this weekend, as a list or on a map.
Ask to join. Once the Host accepts, the exact meeting point and Crew chat open.
Meet the group and check in with the Host's six-character code.
Review the people you met, share Moments, and earn Recognition.

body.p: Until a Host accepts you, an Activity shows only an area about 3 km across. The exact meeting point is visible only to the accepted Crew. Discovery never touches the real address.

Check-in turns "accepted" into "was there", and only people who were there can review each other. The check-in shows someone had the Host's code during the Activity. Happenous is honest that it runs no ID or background checks.

body.sub: Nothing claims more than it can prove

body.p: Badges come from recorded events, and review rates stay hidden until enough people have written one. Buddies form only after you've done something together. There are no one-way follows.

sections.heading: Words are part of the design

body.p: The vocabulary is load-bearing and used the same way in the app, the website and the code. Choosing it was a design decision, because each word sets an expectation about how people relate to each other.

White is the ground everywhere, separated by whitespace and a single hairline, never by tinted panels. There is one brand colour, Happenous Orange, and it appears at most once per screen: on the primary button, the active state, or a count. There are no gradients anywhere in the system.

list: Outfit for headings and the wordmark, Inter for everything else, on a short type ladder from 11px to 32px.
Radii of 16 for cards and sheets, 12 for images and 8 for inputs, with pill-shaped buttons.

Motion in three steps (120, 200 and 320 ms), plus a 480 ms "celebrate" duration reserved for Buddy connections and milestones. It's never used for penalties, and reduced motion is respected everywhere.

body.p: An Expo and React Native app with expo-router, an Express and TypeScript API on PostgreSQL with PostGIS for the location rules, a React moderation console for administrators, and a static marketing site. Everything runs on Google Cloud.
